verdict.rationale: Foreloop documents background autonomy: once set up, an agent checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive, opening PRs. Connected repositories also get automatic product reviews on pull requests. However, the agent must run on the user's own machine via Claude Code or Codex, nothing runs until a person approves a contract, and recurring schedules beyond the agent's polling rely on external cron rather than a first-party scheduler. missing for 10: user-defined automation/trigger configuration, first-party recurring scheduling, hosted background execution without a user-run agent, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
Connect a repository and get automatic product reviews on your pull requests.
That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
Nothing runs until a person approves a contract.
